metadata.summary: The Sleep-EDF (Expanded) database provides full-night polysomnography (PSG) recordings for sleep research. It includes two cohorts: healthy subjects (SC) and subjects with mild difficulty falling asleep (ST). Each recording contains EEG (Fpz-Cz, Pz-Oz), EOG, submental EMG, and event markers, manually scored with the R&K sleep-stage standard.

known_limitations: Data collected 1987–1994 — outdated equipment, protocols, and scoring standards (R&K, not AASM).
Cohort skewed toward healthy and mild insomnia subjects; not representative of general clinical sleep disorder populations.
bias_sources: clinical selection bias (healthy + mild insomnia only)
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: Healthy and mild insomnia subjects only; lacks diversity in severity, comorbidities, age range, and geography.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Limited generalizability to contemporary clinical sleep populations due to temporal, demographic, and methodological drift.
bias_and_limitations.subgroup_coverage: No reporting on sex, ethnicity, or age subgroups.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: No explicit description of missing data patterns.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Cohorts include healthy subjects (SC) and subjects with mild difficulty falling asleep (ST).

population.target_population: Adults with normal sleep or mild insomnia (difficulty falling asleep).
population.inclusion_criteria: Healthy subjects or subjects with mild difficulty falling asleep.
population.missing_groups: General clinical population (e.g., severe insomnia, comorbid psychiatric or neurological disorders) is underrepresented.

annotation.annotation_method: Manual scoring using Rechtschaffen & Kales (R&K) standard.
annotation.labeling_provenance: Manually scored by experts using R&K criteria.
annotation.label_noise_description: R&K scoring is outdated relative to current AASM standards; inter-rater variability not reported.

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Tasks requiring AASM-compliant staging or generalizability to modern clinical insomnia populations.
